title: DataAccessV1dot5
description: K-05 v1.5, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1184, from T-1141's round 1 NEED, item 2; DL-364; QUESTIONS.md CQ-179). It only adds to v1.4 (data-access.v1.4.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to v1.3, v1.2, v1.1 and v1): every v1.4 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes, so every v1, v1.1, v1.2, v1.3 and v1.4 exchange is a v1.5 exchange. It adds no database call and changes no read: readOutboxRow reads as v1.3 says, its recipient's roles as stored. Added: rowReader, the consumers' mapping of README item 35's table row role and FinalizeRow.reader (README item 44), stated as an exchange so its fixtures check it. A row whose recipient holds a role at the row's business is read by that role, as v1.3 maps it; a row whose recipient, a person, holds no role is read by the audience of the step line the row carries when the row's step is in section 1 of its flow, the sign-up section the sign-up door enters (ADR-013 section 3); every other row whose recipient holds no role is still refused (noReader). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

rowReader.request.title: RowReaderRequest
rowReader.request.description: What the reader mapping reads (README item 44; item 35's table, row role and FinalizeRow.reader): from readOutboxRow's answer (v1.3 item 35), the row, its bundle, its line and its recipient, the person and their live roles at the row's business as stored; and from the row's bundle (K-01 v1, through the caller's own bundle port, as item 35's flow row reads it: README default 53), the flow the step is read in, the step's section in that flow and the lane of the step line the row carries. Not a database call: no K-05 read changes, and nothing here comes from PostgreSQL that readOutboxRow does not already answer. New in v1.5.

outboxRowId.description: readOutboxRow.response outboxRowId: the row (K-04 v1 outbox_rows.id).

bundleId.description: readOutboxRow.response row.bundleId: the bundle the row was committed under (outbox_rows.bundle_hash and bundle_build), whose flow graph the flow, section and line are read in (arch 10 line 548; README item 35's table, rows flow and allowedLinks).

line.description: readOutboxRow.response line: the step and line the row carries (rowLine). Never null here: a row whose line is null is refused before a reader is looked for (README item 35's table, rows step and line; default 48).

recipient.description: readOutboxRow.response recipient's person and live roles at the row's business, as stored (K-04 v1 outbox_rows.recipient_person_id; person_roles with ended_at null): the row's own recipient, never another person on the handle (S13-31: the role comes from what the message is about, never the phone alone).

personId.description: recipient.personId: the person the row goes to, or null for a row to a handle with no person, which holds no role and stays refused (README default 64).

roles.description: recipient.roles: the person's live roles at the row's business, in role id order, as stored; empty for no live role there, no business yet or no person (v1.3 rowRecipient.roles).

flow.description: The flow the row's step is read in (README item 35's table, row flow; default 53): an A or B step's own; a shared step's, the booking's for a row about a booking, else the first of A, then B, that the row's bundle lists whose graph holds the step (K-01 v1 flowLetter).

section.description: The step's section in that flow's graph: K-01 v1 step.section, the n of the flow graph's section that holds it (flowGraph.sections; SPEC-master section 1: each flow is the 13 sections of LINES.md, in order). Section 1, '1. Business onboarding', is the sign-up section, which the sign-up door enters (K-02 v1.1 default 9; ADR-013 section 3); a shared step's section is the same in both flows (README default 65).

lineTo.description: The lane the step line the row carries goes to (K-01 v1 message.to, a lane), read with no role to tell it by (README default 62): when every line of the step from Rosie (its say messages from san, MC R1) goes to one lane, that lane; null when they go to two or more lanes, since the row's line.index counts the lines to its reader, which only a role names, or when the step has no line from Rosie at that index. S1-02's one line from Rosie goes to owner (K-01 bundle-v0-skeleton.json).

rowReader.response.title: RowReaderResponse
rowReader.response.description: Who reads the row (README item 44): reader, the K-03 v1 readerRole the composer writes for (composeInput audience.role) and limit 7 checks every field against (FinalizeRow.reader; arch 06 line 311), and where it came from: from roles, the role the message is for among those the recipient holds (roleId; ComposeRow.role is that role: T-308; S13-31), as v1.3 maps it; or from signUpLine, the audience of the step line the row carries on the sign-up section, for a recipient who holds no role (roleId null; ComposeRow.role is the role of the reader's own name, never written or held: README default 63). New in v1.5.

oneOf.title: RowReaderByRole
oneOf.description: Read by a role the recipient holds at the row's business: the one the message is for (T-308; S13-31), through readerOf (owner and admin read as the owner, staff and customer as themselves: actions/src/finalize/claim-check/audience.ts), as v1.3 maps it. A role that reads as no one (own_business) gets noReader instead.

reader.description: readerOf of the role the message is for (K-03 v1 readerRole).

from.description: roles: read by a role the recipient holds.

roleId.description: person_roles.id of the role the message is for, one of the request's recipient.roles.

oneOf.title: RowReaderBySignUpLine
oneOf.description: Read by the sign-up line: the recipient, a person, holds no role at the row's business, the row's step is in section 1 of its flow, and the step line the row carries goes to a reader lane: owner reads as the owner, staff as staff, cust as the customer (K-01 lane to K-03 readerRole: actions/src/compose-input/master-line.ts READER_LANES). README item 44.

reader.description: The reader the line's lane names (K-03 v1 readerRole).

from.description: signUpLine: read as the audience of the step line the row carries, on the sign-up section.

roleId.description: None: the recipient holds no role, and the reading gives them none (README default 63).

noReaderError.title: NoReaderError
noReaderError.description: No one reads the row, so compose input and finalize refuse it, and nothing is composed or sent (README item 44; v1.3 item 35's table: 'with none, refused'; T-1141's noReader). why: noRole, the recipient holds no role at the row's business and the sign-up reading does not apply, since the row's step is outside section 1 of its flow or the row has no recipient person (README default 64); lineHasNoReader, the sign-up reading applies but the step line the row carries goes to no reader (a lane other than owner, staff and cust: K-01 lane) or cannot be told without a role (lineTo null: README default 62); roleReadsAsNoOne, the role the message is for reads as no one (own_business: readerOf). New in v1.5.

rowReader.errors.title: RowReaderErrors
rowReader.errors.description: noReader, the mapping's one refusal. A row whose line is null, and one whose step the row's bundle does not hold, are refused before a reader is looked for (README item 35's table, rows step, line and flow), and a read's own errors (notFound, fixedLineRow, transient) are readOutboxRow's, not this mapping's. New in v1.5.

rowReader.exchange.title: RowReaderExchange
rowReader.exchange.description: README item 44, the consumers' reader mapping (compose input's ComposeRow.role and finalize's FinalizeRow.reader, bound in the Tool API turn face by T-1141), as one exchange so its fixtures check: not a database call, so no database test runs it, and its given says what the row's read assumed. Its rules (dependentSchemas, on outcome) tie the outcome to the request: a recipient who holds a role is read by it, never by the line; one with no role is read by the line's audience only as a person on a section 1 step whose line goes to owner, staff or cust; every other recipient with no role gets noReader. Which of several roles the message is for (T-308) is the caller's, as v1.3 says, and is not checked here. New in v1.5.

outcome.description: README item 44's rules, each tying the outcome to the request. Together they decide every recipient with no role, and leave a recipient with a role to v1.3's mapping by role.

allOf.description: A recipient who holds a role at the row's business is read by it, never by the line: a reader from roles, or noReader when the role the message is for reads as no one (refuse-row-reader-role-read-by-line).
A row with no recipient person holds no role and is no one's own sign-up: noReader, noRole (README default 64).
A recipient who holds no role, on a step outside section 1 of its flow: still refused, as v1.3 refuses it (noReader, noRole; refuse-row-reader-no-role-outside-section-1).
A person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to the owner: read as the owner, by the sign-up line (row-reader-s1-02-no-role).
A person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to staff: read as staff, by the sign-up line.
A person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to the customer (lane cust): read as the customer, by the sign-up line.

A person with no role, on a section 1 step whose line goes to no reader lane (agent, pay, out, other or san) or cannot be told without a role (lineTo null): noReader, lineHasNoReader (README default 62).
